research_concepts: separability of role coverage from talent and possession counts
methodological_questions: Are organizer, shaper and terminal roles defined operationally, and are the definitions fixed before analysis?
Does lineup role coverage vary within team-season after accounting for lineup minutes and possession counts?
Is role coverage separable from talent, or does a talent proxy absorb it?
Do talent controls behave as intended given the role labels are derived from the same play-by-play?
evidence_establishes: No earlier study by this project was returned by retrieve_history for this question (n_results = 0). No prior finding about lineup role coverage, its within-team variation, or talent control is established by the retrieved evidence.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether organizer, shaper or terminal roles have been defined, validated or tested in this project.
Whether the within-team variation or talent-control behaviour claimed in the question holds.
Whether any earlier approach to this question failed, and why.
own_inferences: The question as posed names three roles but does not define them in the task text. Role membership must be operationalised from play-type fields (initiator, play type, points) before any test, and the definition is a researcher choice that could drive the result.
If roles are assigned from points or shot outcomes in the derived play-type records, coverage would partly encode scoring, making the separability claim circular.

Lineup coverage per team-season is a thin unit: 90 team-seasons nested under 420,993 possessions gives moderate possession counts but few independent team-season clusters for between-team talent contrasts.
The 2025-26 playoffs are only complete from 2026-06-21, so any analysis dated 2026-07-13 must use the complete snapshot and label it as such.
uncertainties: No glossary or data-catalog lookup was made, so the exact definitions of the three roles and the talent measure are unknown.
Whether lineup-level role labels are stable across seasons (DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY) is unknown.
How reliable the play-type classification is for role assignment is unknown.
No historical evidence on power, effect sizes or reliability for this construct is available.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no records, so no prior result, failed approach or prior study changed the decision. The decision rests only on the task text and the data description.

blocking_constraints.text: Role labels depend on play-type classification from play-by-play that has not been validated for these roles; misclassification could make coverage effects unrecoverable.
Within-team lineup contrasts across 90 team-seasons may have limited power to separate role coverage from talent once team-season effects are absorbed.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved (retrieve_history returned an empty list), so whether this question has been answered is unknown. No prior work is relied on.

risks.text: If roles are assigned using points or shot results from the derived play-type records, coverage is partly defined by the outcome it is meant to explain.
Coaches choose which lineups play together, so lineup role coverage is not randomly assigned and may track matchups or game state.
Talent is correlated with role coverage; a poor talent proxy leaves residual confounding, and a good proxy may absorb the role effect.
Many lineups have few possessions, so lineup-level role coverage estimates will be noisy and unevenly distributed.
Coverage measured from a single season of lineup possessions may be unreliable across seasons and samples.
Testing three roles, several coverage thresholds and multiple talent specifications invites selective reporting.
Using full-season or full-playoff statistics to define lineups or talent for games already played can leak future information.
Play style and rotation patterns changed across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so pooled estimates may mix regimes.
Ninety team-seasons provide few independent clusters for between-team contrasts, which limits power for the separability claim.

design.estimand: Within-team-season association between lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper or terminal on court) and lineup possession outcomes, conditional on out-of-sample talent and possession counts, with the coverage effect distinguished from talent and counts.
design.unit: Lineup-stint or possession within a team-season, with team-season fixed effects.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season and playoffs using only the complete snapshots (regular season from 2026-04-13, playoffs from 2026-06-21). Total 420,993 possessions across 90 team-seasons.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum possession count per lineup and a minimum number of team-seasons; run a simulation under the assumed effect size and cluster structure before analysis. Report the minimum detectable effect and do not claim separability if power is below a pre-set threshold.
design.controls: Talent measured from a prior-season or out-of-sample source (not the same games); possession counts and lineup minutes; team-season fixed effects; game-state controls; clustering by team-season or game. Role definitions fixed in writing before analysis, with a validation sample on play-type labels.
design.falsification: Placebo role labels (for example, shuffled initiator identity within team-season) and a negative-control outcome should show no coverage effect; a talent-only model should match the coverage model if separability holds.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register the three role tests and a single primary coverage threshold; correct for the remaining specifications or report them as exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Claim within-team variation and separability only if the primary coverage coefficient is distinguishable from zero after talent and count controls, survives the placebo and negative-control checks, and the power simulation meets the threshold. Otherwise report as uncertain or untestable.
design.data_version: Snapshot dated 2026-07-13: 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21; earlier seasons as recorded. Role labels built from play-by-play action, sub-type, and initiator fields only, not from points.

Does talent control behave as intended when estimating role coverage effects?
What measurement reliability and exposure sparsity issues affect lineup-level role coverage?

You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. - glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
